question: At which session did the Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Surat Session**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Surat Session of the Indian National Congress took place in **1907**, marking a significant event in India's freedom struggle.
 
• This session led to a **split between Moderates and Extremists** in the Congress.
 
• The division occurred due to ideological differences—Moderates believed in constitutional reforms, while Extremists advocated for more aggressive measures like boycotts and Swadeshi movements.
 
• Prominent leaders like **Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale** represented the Moderates, whereas **Bipin Chandra Pal, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Lala Lajpat Rai** led the Extremists.
 
• The split weakened the Congress for some years but also reflected the growing intensity of the nationalist movement in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arrival of Simon Commission (1928):**

 
 
• The Simon Commission was a group of British parliamentarians sent to India to recommend constitutional reforms.
 
• It was boycotted by Indians as it did not include any Indian members. The slogan "**Simon Go Back**" became popular during protests.
 
• The commission's arrival significantly fueled the demand for **Purna Swaraj (complete independence)**.
 
 
 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):**
 
 
• Initiated by Lord Curzon, the partition aimed to divide Bengal into East Bengal (majority Muslims) and West Bengal (majority Hindus).
 
• This move was perceived as an attempt to create communal divisions and weaken the growing nationalist movement.
 
• The partition led to massive protests, the **Swadeshi Movement**, and the eventual annulment of the partition in 1911.
 
 
 
• **Formation of the Muslim League (1906):**
 
 
• The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka to promote the political interests of Muslims in India.
 
• It later played a crucial role in the demand for **Pakistan** and the eventual partition of India in 1947.
 
• Initially, the League supported British rule and sought to protect Muslim rights within the Indian framework.
